outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: The Landscape of Language Model Alignment
outline.description: This chapter establishes the foundational problem of steering large unsupervised language models (LMs) to align with human intent. It contrasts broad pre-training capabilities with the difficulty of controlling specific behaviors, introduces the necessity of re-training on relative preferences rather than absolute instructions, and sets the stage for comparing existing methods against an intuitive RL framework.
subtopics: The limitations of unsupervised pre-training: Broad knowledge vs. controlled behavior
The concept of preference data versus instruction-tuning
The standard Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) pipeline: Reward Modeling and Policy Optimization
Practical challenges of RLHF: Computational cost, sampling loops, and stability issues
The motivation for Direct Preference Optimization (DPO): Avoiding explicit reward modeling

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: Theoretical Foundations of Reward-based Policy Optimization
outline.description: This chapter provides the mathematical justification for why DPO works. It contextualizes the approach within classic preference learning theories, defines equivalence in reward functions, and proves that a specific parameterization allows for the closed-form recovery of optimal policies without needing to evaluate a partition function.
subtopics: Foundational Preference Models: The Bradley-Terry model and its application to LLMs
The Reinforcement Learning Objective: Maximize Reward minus KL Divergence constraint
The Optimal Policy Representation: Analyzing Equation 8 ($ rac{ho(x,y)}{ho_{ref}(x,y) eta}$)
The Change-of-Variables Trick: Mapping Reward Functions back to Policies
Proof that equivalent rewards yield equivalent optimal policies (Equivalence Class Lemma)
Why this reparameterization enables an exact solution via Maximum Likelihood

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Mechanics and Optimization Dynamics of DPO
outline.description: This chapter details the internal workings of the DPO algorithm. It moves from abstract theory to practical implementation nuances, explaining how gradients naturally adjust model weights based on preference discrepancies, introduces importance weighting to prevent degradation, and outlines the efficient training loop.
